proof_nl: Let x be any real number. By the defining property of the floor function, floor(x) is an integer with floor(x) ≤ x. Subtracting floor(x) from both sides gives 0 ≤ x - floor(x). Since x was arbitrary, this holds for every real number x. Hence, for all real x, 0 ≤ x - floor(x).
solver_summary: Use the defining inequality floor(x) ≤ x and rearrange to obtain x - floor(x) ≥ 0 for arbitrary real x.
vetter_reason: The proof directly establishes the stated inequality from the defining property of floor: floor(x) <= x, hence 0 <= x - floor(x). It is complete, correct, and exactly matches the lemma statement with no semantic drift.
